outcome: Common web attacks are blocked at the edge while bots are separated from real shoppers, protecting both the application and trading margin.
overview: An online store is attacked in two different ways at once, and they need different answers. Injection and application-logic attacks try to break the application; scrapers, credential-stuffers and inventory bots use it exactly as designed, only far too much. FortiWeb sits in front of the application with a rule set for the first problem, a machine-learned traffic model for anomalies, and bot management for the second, because blocking bots protects margin and stock availability, not just data. Redington tunes it in detection mode against real traffic before anything is enforced.

benefits.text: Common web application attacks are blocked before they reach the application
benefits.limits: A web application firewall reduces exposure to classes of attack; it is not a substitute for fixing the vulnerability underneath, and treating it as one is how it becomes permanent

benefits.text: Automated abuse — scraping, credential stuffing, inventory holding — is separated from real customers
benefits.limits: Bot classification is probabilistic and mis-classification costs real transactions; the tuning period exists precisely because of that

benefits.text: Attack traffic is characterised, so the security team can describe what is actually happening
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Available as an appliance or virtual machine inside the customer estate, so request bodies and customer data need not transit a third-party inspection service

notFor.situation: A storefront already behind a content-delivery network with an integrated web application firewall
notFor.why: Two web application firewalls in the same path double the false-positive surface and halve the clarity about which one blocked a request

notFor.situation: An application with no public interface
notFor.why: The control belongs in front of internet-facing applications; an internal-only service has different exposure

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 6–8 weeks including a detection-mode tuning period that is not compressible
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed tuning with an agreed false-positive threshold.
1) Assessment — traffic profile, payload sizes, peak volumes and current exposure
2) Design — inspection topology, certificate handling, policy set and the enforcement criteria
3) Deploy and tune — detection mode against production traffic, false-positive triage, model learning
4) Enforce and hand over — enforcement enabled against the agreed threshold, operations handed over
deliverables: Every blocked request is traceable to the specific rule, model or bot policy that blocked it
A promotional-event configuration is tested before the event rather than during it
Virtual patches are recorded against the application defect they compensate for
